items.title: Microsoft has changed its product names so many times that there's a website to track them all
items.author: Simon Batt
items.content: If you've been a long-term Windows user, there's a good chance you still have old terminologies and product names rattling around in your head. I admit that I still call any disc-shaped storage medium a "CD," and I still think Windows comes with "Windows Defender" as its default antivirus (it was renamed to "Microsoft Defender" in 2019).

items.title: Linux 7.3 will boost minimum framerates by 7x on older CPUs, which is perfect in this hardware crisis
items.author: Simon Batt
items.content: With the current hardware price crisis biting into every PC gamer's pocket, it feels like we're all hoping and praying that the hardware we bought years ago will last for the next few years. Fortunately, Linux developers are always working to ensure that older chips can run at their best. Such is the case with a new commit that got merged into Linux 7.3, which raises minimum framerates by 7x on an old CPU.

items.title: Microsoft is slowly breaking Windows Media Player Legacy to force people over to the new app
items.author: Simon Batt
items.content: With Microsoft's big Windows K2 initiative in full swing, we're seeing much-needed improvements such as finally making Windows 11's context menus make sense. However, we're also seeing Microsoft push for people to leave its older software behind and embrace its newer versions.

items.title: You can grab a serious gaming mouse for $35 right now, but this deal won't last long
items.author: Timi Cantisano
items.content: The Razer Basilisk V3 is the gaming mouse to get if you want strong performance on a budget. It's comfortable, packed with buttons, and has a 26K DPI optical sensor. Its MSRP is a whopping $70. But you can now get it for 50% less from Amazon, bringing it down to just $35.

items.title: You can grab a curved 31.5-inch Acer Nitro monitor for $190 right now
items.author: Timi Cantisano
items.content: This Acer Nitro 31.5-inch gaming monitor perfectly blends performance and value. It features a 180Hz refresh rate, 1ms response time, and a discounted price of $190. Best Buy is slashing the price by $270, which is well below its MSRP of $460. It's one of the best prices that we've seen.

items.title: GTA 6 leaker's manifesto demands an apology from Rockstar over its "anti-consumerism"
items.author: Patrick O'Rourke
items.content: Cyberleek, the group that has claimed responsibility for the recent substantial () gameplay leak, says they didn't just drop the footage for fun. The group recently published a manifesto calling out video game industry practices it disagrees with and even went so far as to say it plans to target other publishers it views as anti-consumer (via PC Gamer).

items.title: Microsoft is finally adding privacy tools to Windows 11 that block microphone and webcam access to apps
items.author: Simon Batt
items.content: After Microsoft came out of its Copilot-driven stupor earlier this year, we've seen the company focus its attention back on Windows 11. We've already seen the start of its big Windows K2 rollout, which aims to tackle some of the operating system's biggest pain points. Now, it seems the company is also taking note of the privacy concerns people have had with Windows 11, as it is adding a way to disable microphone and webcam access to certain Win32 apps.

items.title: This $30 Scythe CPU cooler handles Intel and AMD's latest chips, and it's 60% off
items.author: Timi Cantisano
items.content: The Scythe Mugen 6 Black Edition CPU cooler is compatible with Intel and AMD's latest chips and delivers impressive cooling with its six-heat-pipe design and two Wonder Tornado 120 fans. If the hardware lineup doesn't sound like much, know this fan moves a lot of air. The MSRP is $75, but you can now get one from Woot for 60% off, down to $30 for a limited time.

items.title: The Razer Seiren V3 Chroma microphone drops by 60%, now coming in at an all-time low of just $52
items.author: Timi Cantisano
items.content: The Razer Seiren V3 Chroma is the microphone you need to take your audio to the next level. It's great for streaming, podcasts, meetings, video calls, and more. While it can be on the expensive side with its retail price of $130, the white model is now on sale at Best Buy for its 60th birthday. Best Buy is taking 60% off to celebrate, dropping it to just $52 for a very limited time. That's the best price we've seen across most major retailers, so grab it while you still can.
